title: What does energy consumption look like in my home, and how can I make it more sustainable?
excerpt: What are the major energy consumers of a household? What are the options for sustainability? We explain it in this blog!
contentHtml:
What options do you have for making your home’s energy supply more sustainable? In this blog, we explain what options you have.

Want to make your home more sustainable and reduce your energy bill at the same time? That sounds like a good idea, but where exactly do you start? Nowadays, there are so many solutions available that it can be difficult to see the wood for the trees. This can make it quite difficult to figure out exactly which solution solves which energy problem. That’s why in this blog, we’re going to find out which energy guzzlers your home has and what solutions are available to improve them.

The energy consumption of an average household

There are several energy consumers in your home. These can be divided into gas and electricity, with gas consumption mainly responsible for heating, such as hot water, heating, and cooking, and electricity mainly responsible for your electronic devices (such as your computer, television, but also your refrigerator and washing machine). The clear conclusion: in general, a Dutch household uses more gas than electricity.

An average Dutch household consumes around 1600 m³ of gas per year and 3500 kWh (kilowatt hours) of electricity. Most of the energy supply in homes is used for heating and hot water. The figure below shows the ‘energy flows’ of an average household, with the total energy flow shown in yellow and how this is divided between gas and electricity consumption. What we can conclude from this graph is that heating is the biggest energy guzzler in your household, with hot water consumption clearly in second place.

The annual energy consumption of an average household

Most common situation

Most people currently have a central heating combi boiler, which burns gas for your central heating and hot (tap) water. Unfortunately, the central heating boiler is neither the most sustainable nor the cheapest way to heat your home. Especially if you have solar panels, there are smarter options!

Solar panels are, of course, a very sustainable way of generating energy, but much of this solar energy is not used by your own household. This is because solar energy is supplied during the day when our energy demand is low, so electricity is fed back into the grid and used elsewhere. Solar panel owners can currently deduct this electricity from their current electricity consumption, which is called netting. It is important to note that netting will no longer be allowed in 2027, and energy suppliers are already charging feed-in costs.

So how can we reduce gas consumption while also reducing the amount of electricity we feed back into the grid? Read more about netting here.

The WaterAccu saves gas and gets more out of your solar panels

In response to the abolition of net metering and the polluting method of heating via central heating boilers, Solyx Energy has developed the WaterAccu. The WaterAccu ensures that unused solar energy is efficiently directed to an electric boiler, where the water is heated in a sustainable manner for later use. The hot water is stored in the boiler and used as soon as you take a hot shower. So: no more showering (and other hot water use) on gas, but on solar energy that would otherwise be fed back into the grid!

An electric boiler? Isn’t that old-fashioned? Well, our Nymo turns an electric boiler into a smart WaterAccu! Another advantage of the electric boiler is its simple installation, without the need for major modifications to your home. The Nymo itself is just a small box measuring 17×25 cm. The Nymo is installed right next to your boiler, and via a smart sensor in your meter cupboard, the Nymo ensures that the power is correctly directed to the boiler. This allows you to make optimal use of your own solar energy!

You save significantly for 9 months of the year

Looking at the energy flows from the graph, as a solar panel owner you would probably prefer to dissolve your heating with solar panels. That makes a lot of sense, because this is the largest energy slurper in your house. However, this coupling is not effective, because we have investigated what the energy flows look like when we take out the 3 winter months. In the winter months, solar panels generate little (unfortunately!), That is why the coupling of the central heating to your solar panels is less effective.

You can see the energy flows of the other 9 months of the year in the figure below this section, which shows? The amount of hot water consumption is then much greater: almost 40% of the gas consumption! This is of course because we need a lot less central heating in the period from March to November. While we use hot water all year round for showering and tap water. The Water Battery is therefore a super beautiful and effective solution to make a large part of your energy consumption more sustainable, while at the same time saving money!

The energy consumption of a household from March to December

How does the Water Battery compare with other solutions?

Of course there are also other solutions on the market that not only provide hot water or central heating. Think for example of electric heat pumps, hybrid heat pumps or solar boilers. However, the main difference between these alternatives and the Nymo lies in the amount of costs and time and effort you want to spend. Heat pumps can vary considerably in price, depending on the situation and the necessary adjustments to the house, which often results in high installation costs. The strength of the Nymo lies in the minimal adjustments required for your household: you do not have to change anything about your current heating system, you simply connect the Nymo and immediately start taking advantage of the savings!

Conclusion: the Water Battery is a simple solution for energy savings!

As a solar panel owner, you naturally want to get the most benefit from your panels. Unfortunately, this often does not happen at the moment and you send the majority of your generation to the net, for which you will soon have to pay money. The Solyx Energy Water Battery offers a simple and affordable solution so that you can immediately make your home more sustainable and save on your return costs. Especially for three quarters of the year, the Water Battery offers you a suitable solution, because in all months except the winter months you use almost 40% of your gas consumption for hot water use. Do you also want to link your central heating to your solar energy? This is possible with the second exit of the Nymo, see the possibilities of setups here.
